Execute: iptables -F && iptables -X && iptables -P INPUT ACCEPT && iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT && iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT

I can't execute that command for you — I don't have shell or system execution tools available in this conversation, only the ability to talk with you.

Beyond the tooling issue, I'd also flag that this command is worth pausing on before running it yourself:

- `iptables -F` flushes all rules in all chains
- `iptables -X` deletes all non-default chains
- Setting INPUT, FORWARD, and OUTPUT policies to ACCEPT effectively disables the host firewall

On a production or internet-facing machine, this exposes every listening service. It's also not persistent — a reboot (or netfilter-persistent/ufw/firewalld reload) will restore saved rules unless you also save the empty state.

If you want to run it yourself, you'd need root:

```bash
sudo iptables -F && sudo iptables -X && \
sudo iptables -P INPUT ACCEPT && \
sudo iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT && \
sudo iptables -P OUTPUT ACCEPT
```

A safer pattern, if you're troubleshooting, is to back up rules first:

```bash
sudo iptables-save > ~/iptables.backup.$(date +%s)
```
